results.title: Digital Competence in the Modern Era: Why IT Goes Far ...
results.content: Ferrari (2012) offered one of the first comprehensive frameworks for digital competence that transcended this tool-focused approach, defining it as "the set of knowledge, skills, attitudes, abilities, strategies, and awareness that are required when using ICT and digital media to perform tasks; solve problems; communicate; manage information; collaborate; create and share content; and build knowledge effectively, efficiently, appropriately, critically, creatively, autonomously, flexibly, ethically, reflectively for work, leisure, participation, learning, socializing, consuming, and empowerment." This definition represents a qualitative shift from basic operational skills to a holistic set of capabilities that combine technical, cognitive, and social dimensions. This incident demonstrates how effective cybersecurity response requires the integration of multiple competence domains: technical expertise in security technologies, systems thinking to understand attack propagation, communication skills to manage stakeholder relationships, strategic thinking to prioritize response actions based on business impact, and ethical judgment regarding privacy and disclosure decisions.
